NEWS: SpaceX just released the full Starship V3 changelog. Launch scheduled for May 19.

This isn't an incremental update. It's a ground-up redesign.

What changed on Super Heavy:

~ 4 grid fins reduced to 3, each now 50% larger and stronger
~ Integrated hot stage removes the disposable interstage shield entirely
~ New fuel transfer tube roughly the size of a Falcon 9 first stage
~ Engine shrouds removed, new inter-engine shielding added
~ CO₂ fire suppression system deleted
~ Moved from 1 quick disconnect to 2 separate propellant loading systems

What changed on Starship:

~ Clean-sheet propulsion redesign with new Raptor startup method
~ Flap actuation changed from 2 actuators per flap to 1 actuator with 3 motors
~ 4 docking drogues added for ship-to-ship refueling
~ Long-duration orbital systems added for cryogenic fluid management
~ ~60 custom avionics units delivering ~9MW peak power
~ ~50 onboard camera views powered by 480 Mbps Starlink connectivity

Raptor 3 thrust: sea-level up from 230 tf to 250 tf

SpaceX Starshield is now the backbone of US military satellite communications.

Most people know Starlink as home internet. Starshield is its classified sibling, built specifically for government and national security use.

What makes Starshield different:

~ Same satellite infrastructure as Starlink
~ Additional high-assurance encryption capable of handling classified data
~ Owned by the US government, controlled by the Department of Defense Space Force
~ Covers land, maritime, stationary and mobile platforms globally

In May 2026, the US Air Force retired its legacy BACN airborne communications network entirely and replaced it with Starshield. Ten times the data throughput at one third the cost.

A Starlink terminal was also installed at the White House complex.

SpaceX didn't just build commercial internet. It became the connective tissue of American national security.




Muskonomy (@muskonomy)

NEWS: Elon Musk confirms he's using Starlink internet on Air Force One

To be clear, it's actually a special government version called Starshield.

Starshield uses the same SpaceX technology as regular Starlink but is built specifically for government and national security use instead of regular consumers.

The key difference is security. While regular Starlink already has strong encryption, Starshield adds extra high-level protection that can handle classified information.

This allows Air Force One to process sensitive government data securely while flying, meeting the strictest security requirements for presidential communications.

ELON MUSK: The Future of AI Compute Lies in Space, Not on Earth.
“Once you think in terms of harnessing the Sun’s power, you realize scaling massively on Earth is impossible. The entire US averages just ~0.5 TW of electricity. A single terawatt—twice that—requires enormous power plants, transformers, and infrastructure that’s extremely hard to build and scale.
Solar is already cheap, but in space it’s ~10x cheaper: constant sunlight, no batteries needed. The moment low-cost access to space arrives, the cheapest and most scalable way to generate AI tokens will be in orbit—by far. In 5 years, it’ll be an order of magnitude easier.
Prediction: We’ll soon launch and operate more AI compute in space each year than the cumulative total on Earth.”
This keeps the key points (Sun’s power scale, Earth limits, solar advantages in space, Colossus reference implied in scaling difficulty, bold prediction) but trims repetition and improves flow for shareability.

"The Earth only receives about half a billionth of the Sun’s energy.  

The Sun is 99.8% of all mass in the solar system… Earth is in the miscellaneous category.  

Earth is like a tiny dust mote in a vast darkness.  

The way to actually scale civilization is to scale power in space."
